season.rationale:
You delivered both season goals. Your 3:08:38 gravel finish is 1 minute 22 seconds inside your target, following your 1:54:03 half marathon in May. That is an excellent return to consistent training, and I’m proud of the work you put behind it.

Your remaining week is for recovery, not another fitness test. Today’s race produced approximately 301 TSS, so give yourself time to absorb the effort before deciding what comes next.

weeks.blockFocus: Rebuild easy aerobic work, running tolerance and strength
weeks.weekRationale:
Your first full week gives you three short runs, three easy rides and two light strength sessions in 5 hours 5 minutes. Cycling supplies most of the aerobic work while your legs rebuild tolerance for running. Your available 8–10 hours is useful capacity, but using it all before you have established consistent training would add fatigue faster than durability.

- Keep all endurance work conversational; this week builds repeatable training, not speed.
- Pair strength with Monday's run and Thursday's ride to preserve Friday as a full rest day.
- Use indoor cycling for the longer early-morning sessions. Wednesday offers the better opportunity for a short outdoor run, provided footing is secure; rainy, near-freezing conditions favour treadmill running on Monday and Sunday.

Approximately 225 TSS gives projected end-of-week ATL around 22, CTL around 5 and TSB around -17, Productive, assuming negligible starting load and completion of your opening ride. The rest day helps you absorb the work before the weekend.

Your sub-2:00 half marathon remains a credible stretch, not a prediction: its required pace is faster than your current threshold pace. Your gravel target also needs substantial rebuilding. This week puts you on the right process for both goals; later benchmarks must establish whether the finishing times are realistic.
